info.title: Neoxa Exchange REST API
info.description:
Private v2 calls take either signed headers (X-NX-Key, X-NX-Timestamp, X-NX-Signature, optional X-NX-Recv-Window) or the plain X-API-Key and X-API-Secret pair. v1 takes the plain pair only.

Generated by `tools/neoxa_openapi.py` from the Neoxa docs page: Neoxa publishes no OpenAPI file. The guide text below is copied from the same page.

## Authentication

Only API keys authenticate v2. A website login never does. There are two ways to present a key, and the same key works with both unless you turn on signed requests only.

#### Signed requests (recommended)

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| X-NX-Key | Your API key (nex_...). |
| X-NX-Timestamp | Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, 1 to 16 digits and nothing else, taken when you send the request. |
| X-NX-Signature | Hex HMAC-SHA256 of the string below, keyed with your API secret. Upper or lower case hex both work. |
| X-NX-Recv-Window | Optional. How many milliseconds from the timestamp the request stays valid. Default 5000, maximum 60000. A value that is 0, empty or not a number falls back to 5000. A negative value is accepted and makes every request fail with TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW. |

The string to sign is four parts joined with nothing between them: the timestamp text exactly as you send it, the HTTP method in capitals, the path including /api/v2 and the query string exactly as sent, then the request body as the raw bytes. A request with no body ends after the path. Sign the bytes you send, not a re-built copy of them: serialise your JSON once and use that same string for the signature and the body.

Worked example (example secret, not a real key):

```
secret      example_secret_0123456789
timestamp   1767225600000
method      POST
path        /api/v2/order
body        {"pair":"BTCB2_USDC","side":"buy","quantity":"0.5","price":"300"}

string to sign (one line, no separators between the four parts):
1767225600000POST/api/v2/order{"pair":"BTCB2_USDC","side":"buy","quantity":"0.5","price":"300"}

X-NX-Signature (hex HMAC-SHA256 of that string, keyed with the secret):
8614a78c7d10cf670c02ee06f6530ee9071277d46d534e5de73ddf7cbc9873b4

A GET with a query string and no body:
1767225600000GET/api/v2/orders/open?pair=BTCB2_USDC
33b8ad59d9c12ab6435bb697ff13aa7852378cac7c12d99ee2d3f890538d5e1b
```

The server refuses a timestamp that is more than the receive window away from its clock (TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW). Call GET /api/v2/time to check your clock. All three headers X-NX-Key, X-NX-Timestamp and X-NX-Signature must be present; if one is missing the request is treated as an unsigned request.

#### Plain headers

Headers:

```
X-API-Key: nex_your_api_key
X-API-Secret: your_api_secret
```

The same two headers as v1. The secret travels with every request, so use HTTPS only and prefer signing. Sending X-API-Key without X-API-Secret is refused as AUTH_FAILED "Authentication required". A key header longer than 256 characters counts against the IP only.

#### Key rules

- A key can do what its access says: Read covers balances, orders and trades; Trade adds placing and cancelling. An IP allow-list applies to signed and plain requests alike, and must list each address exactly.
- Revocation is fast. Turning a key off or revoking it stops it on v2 within about one second.
- Signed requests only: a switch per key under Settings, API keys. When it is on, plain-header requests and plain socket logins with that key are refused with 401 SIGNED_REQUEST_REQUIRED, and they do not count toward the wrong-secret lock. The secret can no longer be used on v1 either. Only keys created with the v2 key dialog can sign; older keys show "Cannot sign" and keep working with plain headers.
- Changing or resetting your password turns your keys off, as on v1.

#### Wrong-secret lock

Twenty wrong secrets from one IP address, or against one key string, start a lock. The window is fixed: it begins at the first failure and lasts 10 minutes, and when 20 fail inside it, plain-header requests from that IP or for that key get 429 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS until the window ends. A correct secret clears the key's count. Only wrong secrets count: an unknown or disabled key, a signed-only key, a banned account or a refused IP do not. The 429 from the lock carries no RateLimit headers.

Signed HTTP requests are not affected by the lock. Every socket login is: signed or plain, each one is checked against the lock, and a wrong signature (BAD_SIGNATURE) counts as a wrong secret. A locked socket login gets v2:error TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS and the socket is disconnected.

Because the count is also kept per key string, anyone who knows your key string (it is not secret) can lock your plain logins and your socket logins for up to 10 minutes by sending wrong secrets. Your signed HTTP requests keep working through that. Another reason to sign, and to turn on signed requests only for keys that run unattended.

## Rate limits

| Limit | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| 600 per minute | Every /api/v2 request, per IP. Reads (orders, trades, balances, fees, stops, single order) and POST /cancel-after are also counted per key. Market data and /time are per IP only. |
| 10 per 10 seconds | Placing orders: POST /order, /order/test, /stop-order and PATCH /order (amend). Each item of POST /orders/batch counts as one. |
| 20 per 10 seconds | Cancelling: DELETE /order, /orders, /orders/batch and /stop-order. A batch or cancel-all counts once. |

Order and cancel limits are counted twice, per IP address and per API key, and the lower allowance wins. Placing and cancelling have no separate per-key 600 per minute bucket; they use the IP bucket plus their own order and cancel buckets. IPv6 addresses are grouped by /56. Going over returns HTTP 429 with code RATE_LIMITED. Every response carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset, so you can slow down before you are refused; a 429 also carries Retry-After. The limits are separate from v1: v2 traffic does not use up your v1 allowance. A rejected request still counts.

The key routes under /api/v2/keys use the website's account limiter instead: 10 per minute. Failed logins have their own lock, described under Authentication.

## Errors

Every v2 error, whatever its HTTP status, is JSON with a stable code and a human message. Branch on code, never on the message text.

Example:

```
HTTP 400
{
  "code": "INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE",
  "message": "Insufficient USDC balance. Need 150.00, have 98.20"
}
```

A few errors carry an extra field next to code and message: DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID adds orderId, and TOTP_LOCKED adds lockedUntil. Inside a batch reply, an item's error is { code, message } without a status.

#### Request and order errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BAD_REQUEST | 400 | A field is missing, malformed or out of range, or the body is not valid JSON. The message says which. Amounts must be plain decimals such as "0.5"; "1,5" and "10abc" are refused. |
| INVALID_CLIENT_ORDER_ID | 400 | clientOrderId is not 1 to 36 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ or -. |
| UNSUPPORTED_TIME_IN_FORCE | 400 | timeInForce other than GTC or IOC (FOK is not supported). A stop order accepts GTC only. |
| INVALID_TIME_IN_FORCE | 400 | A post-only order with timeInForce IOC. Post-only never takes and IOC never rests, so the order could only be cancelled. |
| INVALID_CURSOR | 400 | before is not a nextBefore value from your own results. Drop it and start again. |
| INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE | 400 | Not enough available balance for the order and its fee. |
| POST_ONLY_WOULD_CROSS | 400 | A post-only order would have filled at once against the book or the pool. Reprice one tick behind the touch. |
| PRICE_OUT_OF_BAND | 400 | A sell under 1/5 of the recent market price, or a buy over 5 times it. Usually a typo. |
| MARKET_IMPACT_TOO_HIGH | 400 | A market order would move the price more than its limit allows. |
| MARKET_NO_LIQUIDITY | 400 | Nothing to fill a market order against. |
| MARKET_ORDERS_DISABLED | 400 | Market orders are switched off. |
| MARKET_PRICE_NOT_ALLOWED | 400 | A market order does not take a price. |
| MARKET_SIZE_BELOW_MINIMUM | 400 | The market order is under the pair minimum. |
| MARKET_SIZE_REQUIRED | 400 | A market order needs exactly one of quantity or total. |
| MARKET_TOTAL_BUY_ONLY | 400 | total (spend this much quote) is for buys only. Sell by quantity. |
| ORDER_NOT_OPEN | 400 | On cancel: the order is already filled or cancelled. |
| AMEND_BELOW_FILLED | 400 | On amend: the new total quantity is not above the filled quantity, or fills before the cancel left less than the pair minimum. In the second case the reply has cancelled set and order null: the cancel stands. |
| BATCH_TOO_LARGE | 400 | More than 10 orders in a batch place, or more than 20 ids in a batch cancel. |
| STOP_PRICE_INVALID | 400 | A buy stop is not above, or a sell stop not below, the last trade price, or the pair has no last price yet. |
| STOP_NOT_WAITING | 400 | The stop already triggered, was rejected or was cancelled. |
| CANCEL_AFTER_INVALID | 400 | timeout is not a whole number from 5 to 86400, or 0. |
| STOP_NOT_FOUND | 404 | No such stop order on your account. |
| ORDER_IN_FLIGHT | 409 | The order is being matched at this moment (amend). Retry after a moment. |
| ORDER_NOT_FOUND | 404 | No such order on your account. Another user's order looks the same. |
| PAIR_NOT_FOUND | 404 | Unknown trading pair. Pair names are case-sensitive. |
| NOT_FOUND | 404 | No such v2 path. |
| DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID | 409 | That clientOrderId was used before on your account, ever. The reply carries the existing orderId. |
| PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | 413 | Request body over 1 MB. |
| TRADING_LOCKED | 403 | Trading is disabled on the account; the message gives the reason. Contact support. |
| PERMISSION_DENIED | 403 | The key does not have Trade access. |
| MARKET_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API | 403 | Market orders are not open to this key. Use a limit order. |
| TRADING_PAUSED | 503 | The market or the whole venue is paused. Nothing was placed. Retry later. |
| SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE | 503 | A brief account check failed. Nothing was placed. Retry. |
| INTERNAL | 500 | A server fault. The outcome of the request is unknown: look the order up by clientOrderId before you retry. |

#### Authentication errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API_KEY_REQUIRED | 401 | No X-NX headers and no X-API-Key or X-API-Secret were sent, or a browser session was used. Only API keys authenticate v2. |
| AUTH_FAILED | 401 | Plain headers refused: unknown key, wrong secret, or key not usable. The message is the v1 text (Invalid API key, Invalid API secret, Authentication required). On plain headers this is also how a banned account (403), a refused IP (403) and a closed account (401) arrive, so the status can differ from 401. A key that is turned off or revoked arrives here too, as Invalid API key. |
| BAD_SIGNATURE | 401 | The signature does not match. Check the string to sign byte for byte. |
| TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW | 401 | The timestamp is outside the receive window. Fix your clock or widen X-NX-Recv-Window (up to 60000). |
| KEY_CANNOT_SIGN | 401 | On signed requests and socket logins: unknown key, a key turned off or revoked, or a key created before signing existed. |
| SIGNED_REQUEST_REQUIRED | 401 | A plain-header request or plain socket login on a key set to signed requests only. Sign the request. It does not count toward the login lock. |
| KEY_DISABLED | 401 | A signed request on a key that was turned off or revoked a moment ago. |
| ACCOUNT_CLOSED | 401 | Signed requests and socket logins: the account was closed. |
| ACCOUNT_BANNED | 403 | Signed requests and socket logins: the account is banned. Contact support. |
| IP_NOT_ALLOWED | 403 | Signed requests and socket logins: the address is not on the key's allow-list. |
| TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS | 429 | The wrong-secret lock (20 wrong secrets in a 10-minute window) is on for this IP or key. Wait for the window to end, or sign your HTTP requests. On a socket it also disconnects. |
| RATE_LIMITED | 429 | Over a rate limit. Wait RateLimit-Reset seconds, then retry. |

#### Key management errors (website only)

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AUTH_REQUIRED | 401 | Not logged in. |
| FORBIDDEN | 403 | The website login was refused for another reason, such as a banned account. |
| SESSION_REQUIRED | 403 | Key management needs a website login. An API key cannot manage keys. |
| CROSS_ORIGIN | 403 | The request came from another website. |
| LABEL_RESERVED | 400 | That label is reserved. |
| PASSWORD_REQUIRED | 400 | Creating a key needs your account password. |
| INVALID_PASSWORD | 401 | Wrong password. |
| TOTP_REQUIRED | 400 | Your account has 2FA on: send totpCode. |
| INVALID_TOTP | 401 | Wrong 2FA code. |
| TOTP_LOCKED | 401 | Too many wrong 2FA codes. lockedUntil says when you can try again. |
| KEY_LIMIT | 400 | You already have 5 keys. |
| KEY_NOT_FOUND | 404 | No such key on your account. |
| KEY_CANNOT_SIGN | 400 | On PATCH: the key was created before signing existed and cannot be set to signed requests only. |

#### Socket errors

Sent as a v2:error event with the same code and message fields. See WebSocket v2 for NONCE_REQUIRED, ALREADY_AUTHENTICATED, AUTH_IN_PROGRESS, TOO_MANY_CONNECTIONS and SESSION_REVOKED; the authentication codes above also apply.

## WebSocket v2

Your own orders, trades and balances, pushed as they change. It is a login on the same Socket.IO namespace the public feeds use (/exchange), so market data subscriptions work as documented under API v1. v1 events are unchanged.

#### Login

1. Connect to the /exchange namespace and send v2:hello.
2. The server answers v2:nonce with { nonce }, a one-time string valid for 60 seconds and for a single attempt.
3. Send v2:auth with { apiKey, signature }, where signature is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the nonce text keyed with your secret. Plain login also works for keys not set to signed requests only: { apiKey, apiSecret }.
4. The server answers v2:authed with { userId }. Events start from that moment.

JavaScript (Node 18+, socket.io-client):

```
import { io } from "socket.io-client";
import { createHmac } from "node:crypto";

const socket = io("https://neoxa.exchange/exchange", { transports: ["websocket"] });

socket.on("connect", () => socket.emit("v2:hello"));
socket.on("v2:nonce", ({ nonce }) => {
  const signature = createHmac("sha256", process.env.NEOXEX_SECRET).update(nonce).digest("hex");
  socket.emit("v2:auth", { apiKey: process.env.NEOXEX_KEY, signature });
});
socket.on("v2:authed", ({ userId }) => console.log("logged in as", userId));
socket.on("v2:error", (e) => console.error(e.code, e.message));

socket.on("order", (o) => console.log("order", o.orderId, o.status, o.filledQuantity));
socket.on("trade", (t) => console.log("trade", t.tradeId, t.price, t.quantity));
socket.on("balance", (list) => console.log("balance", list));
```

Worked nonce example:

```
nonce       9f2c41d7a05b83e6c1d94f7a20be5836d1c7e4a9b02f6853ac0d1e97b4f62a38
secret      example_secret_0123456789
signature   7668ad713ea93cc0ad79485681777b0cea1b093fbc2b468de3d75e959533e355

The signature is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the nonce text itself (the 64 characters, as UTF-8), keyed with the secret.
```

#### Events you receive

| Event | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| v2:nonce | { nonce } after v2:hello. |
| v2:authed | { userId } as a string. The login worked. |
| v2:error | { code, message }. A refused login or a revoked session. |
| order | One of your orders changed: the same object as an order from the REST API (orderId, clientOrderId, pair, side, type, timeInForce, postOnly, price, quantity, filledQuantity, remainingQuantity, averagePrice, status, createdAt, updatedAt). Sent when you place, cancel or partly fill an order, and when a resting order of yours is hit. |
| trade | One of your trades: tradeId, orderId (your own side), pair, side, role, price, quantity, total, fee, feeToken, time. Each side gets the trade from its own point of view. |
| stop | A stop order of yours triggered or was rejected. Triggered: { stopId, status: "triggered", orderId }. Rejected: { stopId, status: "rejected", code, reason }, where code is ACCOUNT_INACTIVE, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, NOT_PLACED or another order code. A stop you cancel yourself sends no event. |
| cancelAfter | A cancel-after deadline fired: { fired: true, cancelled, failed, stopsCancelled, stopsError? }. cancelled lists order ids, failed entries are { orderId, code, message }, stopsCancelled lists stop ids. Sent once per fire, after any retries. |
| balance | An array of balance objects (token, available, inOrders, withdrawing, total) for the tokens that just moved. A full snapshot of each token, not a change amount. |

order event:

```
{
  "orderId": "ORD-MU0LPD4A-945957F1",
  "clientOrderId": "bot-0001",
  "pair": "BTCB2_USDC",
  "side": "buy",
  "type": "limit",
  "timeInForce": "GTC",
  "postOnly": false,
  "price": "300.00000000",
  "quantity": "0.50000000",
  "filledQuantity": "0.10000000",
  "remainingQuantity": "0.40000000",
  "averagePrice": "299.80000000",
  "status": "partial",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-26T10:15:02.114Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-26T10:15:02.301Z"
}
```

stop event:

```
{ "stopId": "STP-MU0LQ1X2-9C4E7A10", "status": "triggered", "orderId": "ORD-MU0LPD4A-945957F1" }
```

cancelAfter event:

```
{ "fired": true, "cancelled": ["ORD-MU0LPD4A-945957F1"], "failed": [], "stopsCancelled": [] }
```

balance event:

```
[
  { "token": "BTCB2", "available": "1.40000000", "inOrders": "0.40000000", "withdrawing": "0.00000000", "total": "1.80000000" },
  { "token": "USDC", "available": "880.20000000", "inOrders": "0.00000000", "withdrawing": "0.00000000", "total": "880.20000000" }
]
```

#### What the stream covers

- Balance events cover every change to your wallets: placing, filling and cancelling orders, and also deposits, withdrawals, transfers and anything else that moves a balance. Changes made outside trading are noticed by a check every 2 seconds, so they arrive about 2 seconds late. Changes made while you have no logged-in socket are not replayed; read GET /api/v2/balances after you connect.
- Events are queued per account and sent in order. Under a burst, only the newest state of each order and the newest balance snapshot are kept, so you can miss an intermediate order state. If more than 100 events pile up, the oldest trade events are dropped first, then the oldest order events, so under a very large burst (over about 100 distinct orders at once) even a final order state can be lost. Only the balance snapshot is never dropped; stop and cancelAfter events are not dropped by this rule. When in doubt, reconcile with GET /api/v2/orders/open and GET /api/v2/trades.
- Nothing is replayed on login, and events only flow while at least one of your sockets is logged in. Fetch the current state over REST first, then listen.

#### Limits and revocation

- At most 5 logged-in sockets per key and 10 per account. A login over the limit is refused with TOO_MANY_CONNECTIONS; the socket stays connected for public feeds.
- A socket gets 5 failed logins, after which it is disconnected with TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS. The 20-wrong-secrets lock applies to every socket login, signed or plain. A frame of any kind that fails counts toward the 5, and the next attempt after the 5th is refused. Sending v2:hello again replaces the nonce. If a login has both signature and apiSecret, the signature is used. apiKey, apiSecret and signature are at most 256 characters.
- The server rechecks logged-in sockets about every 10 seconds. If the key is turned off or revoked, you switch the key to signed requests only while the socket logged in with a plain secret, you change your password, or the account is banned or closed, you receive v2:error SESSION_REVOKED and the socket is disconnected.
- Other login codes: NONCE_REQUIRED (send v2:hello first and sign the nonce it returns), BAD_SIGNATURE, KEY_CANNOT_SIGN, ALREADY_AUTHENTICATED, AUTH_IN_PROGRESS, INTERNAL, plus the authentication codes under Errors.

## Moving from v1

v1 stays up and unchanged. Move at your own pace, one endpoint at a time.

| Topic | v1 | v2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keys | Website keys, plain headers. | The same keys. Keys created after v2 launched can also sign; older keys keep working with plain headers. |
| Base path | /api/exchange/..., /api/wallet/... | /api/v2/... for everything in this section. |
| Numbers | JSON numbers in most places. | Decimal strings with 8 places, for every price, quantity, total, fee and balance. Parse them with a decimal type, not a float. |
| Errors | { error } with a free-text message; order calls answer 400 for nearly everything. | { code, message } with a stable code and a real HTTP status. See Errors. |
| Order ids | order_id in snake_case objects. | orderId in camelCase, plus your own clientOrderId. |
| Idempotency | None. A retry after a timeout can place twice. | clientOrderId is unique per account for good. A repeat answers 409 with the first orderId, so a retry is safe. |
| Order lookup | Lists only. | GET /order by orderId or clientOrderId, with the order's trades. |
| Amend | None. Cancel and place again. | PATCH /order reduces in place, or cancels and replaces for you. |
| Batches | None. | POST and DELETE /orders/batch: 10 placements or 20 cancels per call, with a result per item. |
| Time in force | Not offered. | GTC and IOC. |
| Stop orders | None. | Stop-limit orders with no escrow while they wait. |
| Dead-man switch | None. | POST /cancel-after cancels a key's orders when it stops checking in. |
| Fee rates | Not one call per account. | GET /account/fees, with your NEOXEX discount. |
| Cancel all | Not available. | DELETE /orders with scope, pair and side filters. |
| Dry run | Not available. | POST /order/test runs every check, including the pool edge, and places nothing. |
| Paging | offset and next_before. | A before cursor with nextBefore and hasMore on the history endpoints. |
| Order book | Levels mixed with pool levels. | Every level says whether it is the book or the pool, and the pool's first level sits at its true edge. |
| Signing | None. | Optional HMAC signing with a receive window and a signed-only switch. |
| Live updates | No API-key socket login. | v2:hello, v2:nonce, v2:auth, then order, trade, balance, stop and cancelAfter events. Balance events cover deposits and withdrawals too. |
| Rate limits | Per IP. | Per IP and per key, in their own buckets. |

#### What v1 keeps

- Everything outside the v2 list: wallet, deposits, withdrawal history, liquidity pools, dust, the CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap formats and the public market data under /api/exchange.
- Plain-header authentication and its error messages, exactly as documented under API v1.
- Market orders stay allow-listed per key on both versions.

post.description: Places a limit order, or a market order if your key is allow-listed for them. The reply is final: the order as it stands after matching, and the trades it made. Orders match against the book and the liquidity pool in the same way as on the website. Send a clientOrderId so a retry after a timeout cannot place the order twice.

quantity.description: Base amount, a decimal string or number above 0. Required for limit orders. For a market order give exactly one of quantity or total.

price.description: Limit price, above 0. Required for limit orders; a market order takes none.

total.description: Market buys only: the quote amount to spend.

slippageTolerance.description: Market orders only: the worst price move accepted, capped by the market-order limit for API keys.

postOnly.description: true to reject the order if it would fill at once, against the book or the pool. Limit orders only.

timeInForce.description: GTC (default) rests until filled or cancelled. IOC takes what it can at once and cancels the rest, so it never rests; it cannot be post-only. FOK is not supported. Market orders always report IOC.

clientOrderId.description: 1 to 36 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ or -. Unique per account for good.

x-notes: trades lists the fills made while placing; later fills arrive on the socket or from GET /order.
A fill against the liquidity pool reports fee "0.00000000" and feeToken null, because the pool fee is already inside the price.

An IOC order never rests: the reply shows what filled and the order is closed. In a rare database failure its leftover cancel can fail; the order is then kept out of the book and cancelled within about a minute, and until then the reply and GET /order can show it as partial or open. Treat an IOC in that state as closing. An IOC left behind by a restart is cancelled at boot, with a retry every second if that fails.
Strict about numbers: "1,5" and "10abc" are refused, and so are ".5" and "1e-7" written as strings; JSON numbers are fine. side may be any case.
An unknown pair is 400 BAD_REQUEST (Invalid trading pair), not PAIR_NOT_FOUND.
On a market order, the price field of the order object is its protection cap, not a fill price. Read averagePrice.

get.description: One of your orders, with the trades it has made so far (oldest first, up to 1000).

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id. Give exactly one of orderId or clientOrderId.

parameters.name: clientOrderId
parameters.description: The id you chose when placing.

delete.description: Cancels one open or partly filled order and returns it as it is after the cancel. The unfilled escrow goes back to your available balance.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id. Give exactly one of orderId or clientOrderId.

parameters.name: clientOrderId
parameters.description: The id you chose when placing.

patch.description: Changes the size or price of one of your open limit orders. quantity is always the order's TOTAL size, the part already filled included, like the quantity field of the order itself; it is never "the part that is left". A smaller quantity at the same price reduces the order in place: same order id, same queue position, same client id, and the cut part of the escrow is released. A larger quantity or a new price cancels the order and places a new one for the unfilled part (quantity minus filled) at the new price, with the same pair, side, post-only and time in force. Market orders cannot be amended.

orderId.description: The order to amend. Give exactly one of orderId or clientOrderId.

clientOrderId.description: The id you chose when placing it.

quantity.description: New total size. Must be above the filled quantity. Give quantity, price or both.

newClientOrderId.description: Client id for the replacement order only. Ignored for a reduce. Without it the replacement has no client id: the old one stays with the cancelled order and, like every client id, is never reused.

x-notes: A reduce answers { order }. A replace answers { cancelled, order, error } and is NOT atomic: the cancel commits first and stands whatever happens next. If the new order is refused, order is null and error carries the code and message the placement would have given (most often INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, checked only after the cancel frees the old escrow). Read cancelled together with error as "my order is gone and nothing replaced it". If error is INTERNAL the outcome is unknown: check GET /orders/open.

The new order is sized from the order as the cancel found it, so fills that land between your request and the cancel count, and the total traded never exceeds the quantity you asked for. If those fills leave less than the pair minimum, the reply is 400 AMEND_BELOW_FILLED with cancelled set and order null: the cancel stands.

Refusals that can be known beforehand are made before the cancel and leave the order untouched: size limits, a client id already used, the pair or venue paused (TRADING_PAUSED), the price band (PRICE_OUT_OF_BAND) and a post-only order that would cross (POST_ONLY_WOULD_CROSS).
The replacement belongs to the key that sent the amend, not the key that placed the original. It is in that key's cancel-after and scope=key cancel-all from then on.
ORDER_IN_FLIGHT (409) means the order is being matched at this moment; retry after a moment. An amend that changes nothing is BAD_REQUEST. It counts as an order against the 10 per 10 seconds limit.

post.description: Takes the same body as Place an order and runs every check without placing anything or touching your balance: validation, price band, minimums, balance, post-only against the book and the pool edge, and a duplicate clientOrderId. Use it to validate a strategy or to see whether an order would cross.

requestBody.x-body-same-as-description: Exactly the fields of Place an order.

schema.description: Exactly the fields of Place an order.

x-notes: wouldCross is true if the order would fill at once, against the book or the pool.
A passing test does not reserve anything; the real order can still be refused if prices or balances change.

post.description: Places up to 10 orders one after another, each exactly as Place an order would. The HTTP status is 200 whatever happens to the items; every result carries its index and either order and trades, or an error with code and message. Each item counts against the order limit like a single order, so a batch of 10 uses the whole 10 per 10 seconds. When the limit is reached, that item and all later ones come back with RATE_LIMITED and are not sent to the engine.

orders.description: Array of 1 to 10 objects, each with the fields of Place an order. A non-object item refuses the whole request.

items.description: Array of 1 to 10 objects, each with the fields of Place an order. A non-object item refuses the whole request.

x-notes: Items run in order, not in parallel. A failed item does not stop the others. Use clientOrderId on every item: after a timeout, repeat the batch and the items that were placed answer DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID with their orderId.
More than 10 items is 400 BATCH_TOO_LARGE; the item errors are the codes of Place an order.

delete.description: Cancels up to 20 of your orders by order id, client order id or both, one after another. The reply lists what was cancelled and what failed. Anything that is not your own order fails with ORDER_NOT_FOUND. The call counts once against the cancel limit.

failed.message: Cannot cancel order with status: filled

clientOrderIds.description: Array of client order ids. Together with orderIds, at most 20 ids in total.

items.description: Array of client order ids. Together with orderIds, at most 20 ids in total.

x-notes: Each failed entry repeats the id you sent (orderId or clientOrderId) with a code from Cancel an order, possibly INTERNAL. More than 20 ids is 400 BATCH_TOO_LARGE.

delete.description: Cancels your open orders and waiting stop orders. Orders go oldest first, at most 500 per call. If more matched than were handled, hasMore is true: repeat the call until it is false. Do not read a capped reply as "everything is cancelled". One order failing does not stop the rest; it is listed in failed.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Only buy or only sell orders.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: account (default): every open order on the account, whoever placed it. key: only orders placed with the key making this call.

x-notes: Each entry in failed is { orderId, code, message }, with the codes of Cancel an order and possibly INTERNAL. side must be lowercase buy or sell here.

Your waiting stop orders that match the same filters (scope=key: the key's own) are cancelled first, all of them, and listed in stopsCancelled. hasMore is about open orders only. If the stops could not be cancelled the orders still are, and the reply carries stopsError { code, message }: call again.
If a stop of yours is triggering at that moment the call waits for it, up to 5 seconds, so the order it places is cancelled with the rest.
The call counts once against the cancel limit.

post.description: A stop-limit order. While it waits nothing is reserved and nothing is in the book: no balance is checked and it does not show in your order lists, on the website or on v1. When the last trade price of the pair reaches stopPrice, the limit order (limitPrice, quantity, GTC) is placed for you and the balance is checked then. A buy stop must be above the last price and a sell stop below it, otherwise place a plain limit order. The same fields and checks as Place an order apply to pair, side, quantity, limitPrice, postOnly and clientOrderId. Market and IOC stops are not supported.

stopPrice.description: The trigger. A buy stop triggers when the last trade price is at or above it, a sell stop when it is at or below it.

limitPrice.description: The price of the order that is placed.

postOnly.description: The placed order is post-only. If it would cross at trigger time the stop is rejected.

clientOrderId.description: 1 to 36 characters as for orders. Reserved for good, shared with your orders: it cannot be used again after the stop is cancelled, rejected or triggered. The triggered order is placed under it.

x-notes: The last trade price is read every 500 ms. A spike that crosses the stop price and comes back between two reads does not trigger it.
Anyone who trades through the book on a thin pair can move the last price. The limit price bounds your fill, so choose a limit you are content to trade at.

Without a clientOrderId the order is placed with the stop id (STP-...) as its clientOrderId, so GET /order?clientOrderId=<stopId> always finds it. The stop id and client id are also refused as a clientOrderId for any order of yours.
The order is placed under the key that placed the stop, so it is in that key's cancel-after and scope=key cancel-all.

At most 50 waiting stops per account (BAD_REQUEST). A pair with no trade yet has no last price (STOP_PRICE_INVALID). If trading is paused when a stop is hit, it waits and triggers after the pause. In the rare case of more than 1000 waiting stops across all accounts at once, the newest wait an extra read or more.
The limit price faces the same price band as an order, checked now and again at trigger time.

get.description: One of your stop orders. Once it has triggered, triggeredOrderId is the order it placed. A rejected stop carries the reason in rejectReason.

parameters.name: stopId
parameters.description: The stop id. Give exactly one of stopId or clientOrderId.

parameters.name: clientOrderId
parameters.description: The client id you gave the stop.

x-notes: status is waiting, triggered, rejected or cancelled. A stop is rejected when, at trigger time, the account is banned, closed or trading-locked, or the key is disabled, deleted or lost Trade access (ACCOUNT_INACTIVE), when the balance is short (INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE), or when the order is refused for another reason such as POST_ONLY_WOULD_CROSS or PRICE_OUT_OF_BAND. A stop caught by a server restart before its order was placed is rejected with NOT_PLACED; it is never placed late, so place it again.

delete.description: Cancels a waiting stop. A stop is either cancelled or triggered, never both: if it has already triggered, rejected or been cancelled the answer is STOP_NOT_WAITING and its order, if any, is cancelled with Cancel an order.

parameters.name: stopId
parameters.description: The stop id. Give exactly one of stopId or clientOrderId.

parameters.name: clientOrderId
parameters.description: The client id you gave the stop.

get.description: Your stop orders, newest first. hasMore is true when older stops matching the filters exist beyond the page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Stops per page, 1 to 500 (default 500). Another value is refused, not clamped.

post.description: Sets the key's deadline to now plus timeout seconds. Call it again before the deadline to push it out: a bot calls it on a timer, for example every 10 seconds with a timeout of 60, so only a bot that has stopped talking loses its orders. If the deadline passes without a re-arm, every open order this key placed is cancelled, without a cap, together with the key's waiting stop orders, and the key is disarmed. Orders of other keys and of the website are not touched. A timeout of 0 disarms.

timeout.description: Whole seconds, 5 to 86400, or 0 to disarm. A digit string is accepted; fractions, signs and anything else are refused.

x-notes: The deadline is kept in the database, not in a timer. One that passes while the server restarts fires on the first tick afterwards, so every open order of the key is cancelled at boot. Use a timeout of tens of seconds at least, and re-arm as soon as you reconnect. Deploys are announced.
A re-arm that arrives after the deadline does not stop a sweep that has already started; orders it has cancelled stay cancelled, and the new deadline is kept.

If a cancel fails for a reason other than the order already being closed, the sweep is tried again every second. It is given up on, and logged, only after 5 tries and 60 seconds since the first failure.
When it fires, a cancelAfter event is sent to your logged-in sockets (see WebSocket v2). The orders a stop places and an amend's replacement belong to the key that sent them, so they are covered too.
armed is authoritative: secondsLeft rounds, and under one second can read 0 while still armed.

get.description: The key's current state. When it is not armed, deadline and secondsLeft are null.
Your open and partly filled orders, newest first, up to 500. No paging; if you could have more, cancel or filter by pair.

Your filled and cancelled orders, most recently finished first. To page, pass the nextBefore from one page as before on the next, and stop when hasMore is false. The cursor is an order id from your own results; any other value is refused with INVALID_CURSOR, so on that error drop the cursor and start again. Paging stays correct while new orders finish between calls.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: Orders that finished at or after this time. Epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 date.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: Orders that finished at or before this time.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Cursor: the nextBefore of the previous page.

x-notes: before may be the id of any of your own orders, open ones too; results start after that order's position.
limit must be a positive integer; values above 500 are lowered to 500, not refused.
startTime and endTime filter on when the order finished (filled or cancelled), the same time the list is sorted by.

get.description: Your trades across all pairs, newest first. Each row is your side of the trade: role says maker or taker, and side is what you did. Page with before and nextBefore as for order history; the cursor here is a tradeId from your own results.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Cursor: the nextBefore of the previous page.

x-notes: limit works as for order history.
There is no pair filter on trades. Filter on pair in your own code.

get.description: Every token you hold or have an order in. inOrders is held by your open orders, withdrawing is locked by pending withdrawals, and total is the three added up.
x-notes: Sorted by token. Tokens with a zero balance are included.

get.description: The maker and taker fee rate of every pair, and your NEOXEX holding discount. The fee you pay on a fill is the rate times (1 - neoxexDiscount). The same rates the engine charges; fills against the liquidity pool report no fee because the pool fee is in the price.
x-notes: neoxexDiscount follows your available NEOXEX balance. While tiersPaused is true it is 0 for everyone.

get.description: The book with the liquidity pool shown as part of it. Every level has a source: book for resting orders, pool for the pool. The pool's first level sits at its true edge, the price where the pool starts to fill, not 0.5% away as the v1 ladder starts; the levels after it are the pool's published ladder. bestBid and bestAsk include the pool's edge, so they are the prices you would actually trade at. If a resting order of yours crosses the pool edge the book can read crossed for a moment until it clears.
x-notes: pool is null for a pair with no pool. timestamp is a number, in milliseconds. depth above 500 is lowered to 500.
Pool levels are not guaranteed: when the pool ladder would cross the resting book it is left out of bids or asks, though bestBid and bestAsk still include the pool edge.

get.description: The two prices at which the pool starts to fill, from the same function the order checks use. A buy at or above buyEdge crosses the pool; a sell at or below sellEdge does. A post-only order on the wrong side of these is rejected with POST_ONLY_WOULD_CROSS. buyEdge is reserveQuote / (reserveBase x (1 - feeRate)) and sellEdge is reserveQuote x (1 - feeRate) / reserveBase.
x-notes: For a pair with no pool, buyEdge and sellEdge are null and the other fields are left out.

get.description: The server clock. Use it to check how far your own clock is from the server before you sign requests.
Your API keys. Secrets are never returned.

post.description: Creates a key that can sign. The secret is returned once and cannot be shown again. Needs your password, and your 2FA code if 2FA is on. Up to 5 keys per account.

permissions.description: Array of read, trade or withdraw (default read). Nothing under /api/v2 withdraws, and withdrawals still need rules granted by the operator, so withdraw alone adds nothing.

items.description: Array of read, trade or withdraw (default read). Nothing under /api/v2 withdraws, and withdrawals still need rules granted by the operator, so withdraw alone adds nothing.

ipWhitelist.description: Comma-separated addresses the key may be used from. Empty means any.

totpCode.description: Your 6-digit 2FA code, required when 2FA is on.

patch.summary: Turn a key on or off, or require signing
patch.description: Changes a key. enabled turns it off or on. signedOnly makes the key refuse plain headers and plain socket logins, which is the quick answer to a leaked secret: signed requests keep working, anything holding only the secret stops. Send at least one of the two.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The key's id from List keys.

signedOnly.description: true or false. Only keys that can sign (canSign) accept it.

x-notes: GET /keys has no origin check; POST, PATCH and DELETE refuse other sites (requests without an Origin header, such as curl, pass).
The change bites on v2 within about a second. The v1 servers cache keys for up to a minute, so the same change reaches v1 within that minute.

delete.description: Deletes a key for good. It stops working on v2 within about a second.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The key's id from List keys.

get.description: CoinGecko/CMC-compatible market summary for all trading pairs. Returns 24h stats, bid/ask, and volume data.
Returns all trading pairs with their configuration including base/quote tokens, status, and AMM info.
Returns 24h ticker data for every trading pair: last price, change, volume, high, and low.
Returns detailed ticker for a single pair including best bid/ask and spread.

Returns current order book (bids and asks) for a pair, including AMM-generated depth. Levels marked isAmm are generated from the liquidity pool, not resting orders. Resting levels may also carry an orders count. The depth actually used is echoed back in the response.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Price levels per side (default 50). Values are clamped to 1-1000.

get.description: Returns the most recent trades for a pair, ordered newest first.
Returns OHLCV candlestick data for charting. Supports multiple time intervals.
Returns aggregate platform statistics: total trades, 24h volume, active pairs, users, and AMM liquidity.

Returns current USD prices for native currencies (via CoinGecko) and derived prices for all traded tokens. The response is a single object keyed by token symbol and covers every listed token; the example below is trimmed to a few entries.

Returns the AMM liquidity pool state for a pair. spotPrice is reserveQuote divided by reserveBase, the pool price before fees, and is 0 while the pool is empty; K is the constant product reserveBase x reserveQuote; feeRate is the fraction the pool charges on a swap (0.003 = 0.30%). bootstrapReferencePrice is non-null only for an empty pool, where it is the price the first deposit will be held to. Responds 404 when the pair does not exist.
CoinGecko-compatible endpoint. Returns all trading pairs with ticker_id, base, and quote.
CoinGecko-compatible endpoint. Returns 24h ticker data for all pairs. All values are strings.
CoinGecko-compatible endpoint. Returns bids and asks as arrays of [price, quantity] string pairs.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Price levels per side. A smaller value trims the book; it never has more than 50 levels per side

get.description: CoinGecko-compatible endpoint. Returns recent trades grouped by type (buy/sell). All values are strings.
CoinMarketCap-compatible endpoint. Returns market summary for all pairs keyed by pair name.
CoinMarketCap-compatible endpoint. Same as summary, keyed by trading pair.
CoinMarketCap-compatible endpoint. Returns info for all traded assets including withdrawal/deposit status and fees.
CoinMarketCap-compatible endpoint. Returns bids and asks as arrays of [price, quantity] string pairs.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Price levels per side. A smaller value trims the book; it never has more than 50 levels per side

get.description: CoinMarketCap-compatible endpoint. Returns recent trades for a market pair.

Returns all token balances for the authenticated user. Funds reserved by your open orders are taken out of available and shown in in_orders; total is available + locked and does not include them, so your full holding is total + in_orders.
Returns orders for the authenticated user, newest first.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: "active" for open and partial orders; any single status to filter on it; omit for all

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's filled and cancelled orders, most recently updated first. Open and partial orders are NOT included; use Active Orders for those.

Returns the authenticated user's liquidity pool position for a pair. baseValue and quoteValue are the current redeemable value of the LP shares; earnedBase and earnedQuote are that value plus everything already withdrawn, less everything deposited. Returns hasPosition:false when the user holds no shares.

200.description: OK. The docs example is not valid JSON; see x-example-text.

post.description: Place a new limit order. Requires "trade" permission. The order is matched immediately against the order book and AMM if liquidity is available. Pass postOnly:true for maker-only behaviour: the order is rejected rather than filled if it would match on arrival. Market orders over the API are not open to every key: from a key without that access, a request with type:"market" gets HTTP 403 with code MARKET_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API. Price protection: on markets with at least 10 trades by at least 3 different traders in the last 24 hours, a sell priced below 1/5 of the recent market price, or a buy above 5 times it, is refused with code PRICE_OUT_OF_BAND.

200.description: OK. The docs example is not valid JSON; see x-example-text.

postOnly.description: Optional. true = maker-only: the order is REJECTED rather than filled if it would match immediately, against either the order book or the AMM pool. Must be a real boolean; a string is refused. The pool trades closer to the middle than the AMM rows in the order book show, so price against the pool edge, not only the book: from GET /api/exchange/pool/:pair, buy edge = reserveQuote / (reserveBase x (1 - feeRate)) and sell edge = reserveQuote x (1 - feeRate) / reserveBase. A post-only buy must be below both the best ask and the buy edge; a post-only sell must be above both the best bid and the sell edge. Exactly AT an edge is rejected. The error message gives the price it was refused at, so you can step one tick back from it. Omit for normal behaviour.

delete.description: Cancel an open or partially filled order. Requires "trade" permission. The reserved funds go back to your available balance. success:true means the order is now cancelled; the order object in the reply is the order as it stood just BEFORE the cancel, so its status still reads open or partial. Errors: "Order not found", "Cannot cancel order with status: filled" and similar.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's trade history with maker/taker role and fees, newest first. For older trades pass the response's next_before as before; repeat until has_more is false. There is no limit on how far back you can page.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Cursor: the next_before value from the previous page (a trade_id from your own history)

get.description: Your current deposit address for each chain, keyed by chain name. Chains whose deposits are closed are left out of addresses and listed in closedChains with the reason. Only chains where you have already generated an address are listed. For XRP, addresses.xrp is your destination TAG, not an address: send to the exchange XRP address shown on the website deposit page and include this tag.

Your deposits, newest first, with confirmation progress. deposit_state is "confirming" (waiting for confirmations), "confirmed" (enough confirmations, being credited) or "credited" (in your balance). required_confirmations can be null for a chain with no fixed number. For older deposits pass offset; hasMore says whether another page exists. Rows may carry other fields; rely only on the ones shown.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of newer deposits to skip, for paging

get.description: Your withdrawals, newest first. amount is what the address receives; fee is charged on top. tx_hash appears once the withdrawal has been sent. status is one of pending, approved, processing, completed, rejected (also shown when you cancel one yourself) or failed. Rows may carry other fields; rely only on the ones shown.

Every liquidity pool position you hold. baseValue and quoteValue are what your share is worth now; pnlBase and pnlQuote are that value plus everything withdrawn, less everything deposited. poolShare is a fraction (0.0412 = 4.12%).

ErrorV2.description: v2 error: a stable code and a message.

ErrorV1.description: v1 error: free text under `error`. Order calls answer 400 for nearly everything.
